column1: # One row per case, five tab-separated columns:
#   fixture   the envelope in this suite's fixtures/, or `-` for a run that must be
#             refused before either stand-in is reached
#   args      what this case adds to the invocation; a NAME=value word is put in the
#             run's environment instead, which is how a case reaches a stub's refusal
#   exit      the status the caller reads: 0 an answer, 2 a call this script cannot act on
#   expect    `|`-separated fragments the output must contain
#   note      what the case is here to hold

column5: an update landed mid-session: read the installed tree, and diff it against the loaded one
the predecessor is the highest version STRICTLY below the loaded one, never itself
versions rank by semver, not alphabetically (0.9.0 sorts above 0.10.0 as text)
the registry answers for every project on the machine: another project's pin is not this session's
a project record whose directory holds this run does apply, and a stranger's does not
a disabled install is not one a restart loads, whatever version it carries
a cache directory is shared between projects: another project's record is not this session's

column4: installed=0.41.0|installs apply here and disagree|user:0.41.0, project:0.48.0
column5: installs that disagree are both named: which one a restart loads is the host's, not this script's
a record whose path IS the loaded tree says what this project resolved to — evidence, not a ranking
a pinned floor outranks what the script would infer, and resolves to its own tree

column4: floor=0.28.0|floor_root=unknown|the pin has nothing left to diff against
column5: a pin whose tree the cache no longer holds buys no diff, and says so
a symlinked project applies; and with no evidence of which install loads, reload stays unknown
an installed copy at the same version is a different tree — the working copy still reads itself
a plugin of the same name in another marketplace is a different plugin
the registry carries the path it installed to; reconstructing one names the wrong tree
a fallback to the loaded tree says so: silently re-reading it is a diff against itself
prerelease fields compare one at a time, numerically: beta.10 is above beta.2
a tree the host did not install reads itself: nothing swaps it under the session

column4: predecessor=unknown|no earlier version is left in the cache|floor_source=none
column5: a swept predecessor is an ordinary answer, not a failure
the registry could not answer: the cache holds candidates, never the installed version

column4: installed=unknown|did not answer a JSON list
column5: output that is not a JSON list is a reason, not a parse that yields nothing
an unreachable forge never reads as agreement with what is installed
an upstream behind the installed version is not an update waiting — and the mismatch is named
a marketplace pinned to a ref is answered by that ref, not by the default branch
a checkout that only sits inside a repository is never fetched through
a source that is not a path in the marketplace repo falls back to the entry's own version
a marketplace no longer configured leaves upstream unknown, with the reason
a flag without its value is a call this script cannot act on, before any stand-in runs
an unknown flag stops rather than being read as a root
a directory holding no manifest is a caller's mistake, not an unknown version
